chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hilal, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about a child who steals. He said: “If he is seven years old or younger, it is waived from him. If he repeats it after seven years, his fingertips are cut, or they are rubbed until they bleed. If he repeats it, then that which is below his fingertips is cut from him. If he repeats it after that, and he has reached nine years, his hand is cut. And no hadd from the hudud of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is neglected.”

key_terms.حُدُودِ اللَّهِ: the divinely ordained legal limits and punishments of Allah
key_terms.رُفِعَ عَنْهُ: liability or penalty is waived from him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Tahdhib al-Ahkam on a child who steals?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling concerning a child who commits theft, describing graduated disciplinary measures according to age and repetition of the offense. It reflects the treatment of criminal liability and the implementation of hudud within the framework of Islamic jurisprudence.
